With infrequent measurements and information scattered across providers, the full picture is hard to see. Answers arrive late, costs rise, and patients are left navigating the gaps to get the care they need.

Built to learn from test results and clinical outcomes to improve disease detection and risk prediction over time.
Built to improve cancer detection and risk prediction
Help the right patients reach the right care sooner. Reduce unnecessary referrals and workups while prioritizing patients who need further evaluation.

Blood in the urine can signal bladder cancer, yet many patients never receive the recommended evaluation. For those diagnosed, the risk of recurrence can mean years of monitoring and repeated invasive procedures.
What we learn in bladder cancer will help us extend this approach across urology and into other areas of care.

Despite coming from different fields, we share the belief that the biggest advances in medicine will come not just from developing better treatments, but from improving early detection and optimal intervention. We founded Numen on the conviction that making accurate testing accessible at the point of need will transform the field of modern medicine.

We love seemingly intractable interdisciplinary problems. Building Numen requires us to push the boundaries of semiconductor physics, biochemistry, hardware engineering, machine learning, and clinical science. We are assembling an exceptionally talented team united by a shared commitment to turning scientific breakthroughs into a product that doctors, patients, and healthcare systems trust.

We know there’s still a great deal to discover, prove, and build, but we’ve both seen what a difference early detection and timely intervention can make. We have decided that winning the fight against cancer is worth a lifetime of hard work.
We pursue problems others shy away from. No matter the complexity, difficulty, or time it takes, because the hardest problems are the ones most worth solving.
We make the previously impossible feel so obvious, people wonder why it was ever done differently.

Our team has built cancer detection assays, trained clinical prediction models, designed biosensors, and shipped hardware at scale across institutions and companies that define the standard of excellence in each field.

MicroPort Neurotech receives Japanese marketing approval for Numen coil embolisation system

MicroPort Neurotech today announced that it has received marketing approval issued by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan for its independently developed Numen coil embolisation system—marking the first approved product in Japan for the company.

Numen is classified as a Category IV high-risk medical device with special control and experience-demanding requirements during the registration process. As a self-developed, designed and manufactured neurointerventional product, it has been approved by the Japanese authority for its “highly innovative clinical design and excellent performance”, according to MicroPort NeuroTech.

The company claims that it permits stable framing, and smooth filling and finishing, with superb conformability to shapes of aneurysms. Its specifications with different diameters, lengths and softness levels provides physicians with “a full range of embolisation options” to ensure safety and efficacy in all stages of the coiling procedure, MicroPort NeuroTech also says.

The Numen coil embolisation system and NumenFR coil detachment system were approved for marketing in China in 2020, before their first overseas implantations in August 2021. They have further received CE-mark certification in the EU, marketing approval from US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and regulatory clearances in South Korea and Brazil.

MicroPort NeuroTech recently announced that its Numen system had been successfully used in the first two implantations in Poland, with the device’s pushability and detachability being “highly appreciated” by the physicians involved.

Net Blow up is a further development of the Net project both in means of construction and appearance. The object is inflated till the outer surface reaches adequate tension for stretching the nets connected on the inner side of the object. This construction excludes any use of additional structure.

The result is a soft object which deforms and mutates with every movement of its temporary habitants. The outer membrane acts both like a "soft box" diffuser of the outside light, or a projection screen in case of inner illumination of the installation. Cover foto by Tomohisa Tasho

"Hoslow tells his tale in blood." Having spoken so eloquently, he was somehow won over by Volcano Manor, the very place he should have been seeking revenge against. Moreover, he could never bring himself to stain his smooth hands with blood, and in his despair, he arrived at the village where the jars cherish flowers. Even though he had wanted to be a hero, just like the brother he admired.
And so, the brave warrior Little Jar sets out on a journey. Leaving behind the resolution that "Hoslow tells his tale in blood," and a single question for us.

Why would he have a rune belonging to someone related to Queen Marika? As everyone who has played this game knows, the phrase "outside the Lands Between" carries a super-mysterious, dangerous ring to it, like the Greater Will at the edge of the universe, the Elden Beast, or the Two Fingers.
That is, he possessed the Numen's Rune precisely because he failed to become a hero. The Numen's Rune is positioned one rank below the Hero's Rune in terms of rune acquisition.
Certainly, at first glance, it reads as if the Night of the Black Knives was carried out by the "Black Knife Assassins," a group of Numen who are descendants of the Eternal City.
